claim: Staining pattern and intensity are not considered in Ki67 scoring; nuclear and mitotic spindle staining are included
chunk_text: Ki67 immunohistochemical staining serves as a surrogate marker for cellular proliferation in breast cancer, particularly used to classify luminal ER-positive tumors into luminal A and B subclasses. claim: In hormonal therapy-treated cohort, high PHH3 not associated with distant metastasis
chunk_text: This chunk reports comprehensive analysis of PHH3 (phospho-histone H3) expression as a prognostic biomarker in breast cancer. PHH3-positivity was significantly associated with aggressive clinicopathological features including higher tumour stage (P = 0.01), tumour size ≥ 2 cm, high grade, nuclear pleomorphism, few tubule formations, and poor Nottingham Prognostic Index (P < 0.001) [S2]. PHH3 score showed a strong positive correlation with mitotic count per 3 mm² (r = 0.738, P < 0.001) and weak positive correlations with Ki67 score (r = 0.269, P = 0.01; r = 0.177, P = 0.016) [S3, S4]. Univariate survival analysis demonstrated that PHH3 mitotic figures > 20 per 3 mm² were associated with significantly shorter breast cancer-specific survival (BCSS) and distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS), with hazard ratios of 9.42 (95% CI 3.97–22.35; P < 0.001) and 8.53 (95% CI 3.81–19.09; P < 0.001), respectively [S5]. In the nonchemotherapy-treated cohort, high PHH3-stained mitotic cells were predictive of distant metastasis (P < 0.001), but this association was not observed in chemotherapy-treated patients [S6, S7]. Similarly, in the nonhormonal therapy-treated cohort, high PHH3 predicted higher risk of death from breast cancer and distant metastasis (both P < 0.001), but these associations were absent in hormonal therapy-treated patients [S8, S9]. In multivariate Cox regression analysis including tumour grade and nodal stage, PHH3 remained an independent predictor of shorter BCSS (HR 2.568, 95% CI 1.05–6.28; P = 0.039) and worse DMFS (HR 2.87, 95% CI 1.24–6.67; P = 0.014) [S10].

claim: Ki-67 expression scored low if staining observed in <10% of tumour cell nuclei
chunk_text: This chunk describes standardized immunohistochemical (IHC) and in-situ hybridization (SISH) scoring protocols for breast cancer biomarkers. HER2 positivity is defined by SISH score >6 or IHC 3+ [S1]. ER and PR positivity are defined by ≥1% nuclear staining [S2]. Triple-negative (TN) subtype is assigned when tumours are negative for ER, PR, and HER2 [S3]. Basal-like TN tumours are identified by ≥1% positivity for EGFR, CK14, or CK5/6 [S4]. Ki-67 expression is scored as high (≥10% staining) or low (<10% staining) [S6]. TTK and c-Kit are scored on intensity alone using a 0–3 scale (0=negative, 1=weak, 2=moderate, 3=strong) [S7, S8]. p53, vimentin, and AR are scored using an IHC score derived from intensity × percentage of tumour cell staining [S9], then converted to binary classifications: p53 (≥60=positive), AR (>0=positive), and vimentin (>0=positive) [S10].

claim: MAGE-A may inhibit p53 function by blocking p53–chromatin interaction, preventing regulation of tumour cell proliferation and apoptosis
chunk_text: This chunk discusses the molecular and immunohistochemical relationships between cancer-testis antigens (CTAs), p53, chromosomal instability (CIN), and tumour differentiation in breast cancer. p53 mutations produce a stable non-functional nuclear protein that mimics overexpression by IHC, making p53 IHC overexpression a surrogate for functional abrogation [S1|PMC6635746_HIS-73-68|69992]. p53 inadequacy contributes to CIN and aneuploidy [S2], which in turn promotes aberrant DNA damage repair and mutagenesis [S3]. NY-ESO-1-positive tumours show coexpression with p53, implying chromosomal abnormalities and a proliferative advantage [S4]. In contrast, MAGE-A shows no association with p53 [S5], possibly because MAGE-A inhibits p53 function by blocking its interaction with chromatin [S5]. MAGE-A expression is strongly associated with mitosis-independent TTK expression, a spindle assembly checkpoint protein and CIN marker in TNBC [S6]. CTA re-expression is thought to confer stem cell-like properties [S7], and both NY-ESO-1 and MAGE-A show striking coexpression with the luminal progenitor marker c-Kit [S8] and enrichment with vimentin [S9], suggesting primitive differentiation states. Basal-like breast cancers frequently exhibit luminal progenitor-like phenotypes and may originate from this cell type [S10].

claim: MAGE-A and NY-ESO-1 expression both strongly associated with triple-negative phenotype (P < 0.0001)
chunk_text: This chunk from PMC6635746_HIS-73-68 reports on cancer/testis antigen (CTA) expression — specifically MAGE-A and NY-ESO-1 — in an unselected cohort of 367 breast tumours (65 triple-negative [TN]) assessed by IHC on tissue microarrays [S8]. Overall, MAGE-A was expressed in 13% and NY-ESO-1 in 3.8% of all cases [S5, S9], but expression was markedly enriched in TN breast cancer (~47% and ~17%, respectively) [S9]. Both CTAs were strongly associated with the TN phenotype (P < 0.0001) [S6], and NY-ESO-1-positive cases co-expressed MAGE-A (P = 2.06 × 10⁻⁹) [S6]. CTA-positive tumours were the most proliferative and poorly differentiated, showing genomic instability [S6], and were characterised by co-expression of c-Kit and TTK and overexpression of p53 [S7]. Approximately 85% of positive cases showed homogeneous staining (>75% of tumour cells) [S5], supporting IHC of tissue biopsies as a reliable companion biomarker [S10]. The authors conclude that targeting MAGE-A and NY-ESO-1 via immunotherapy is feasible in TN breast cancer [S9].

claim: Mixed tumours -> classified as ductal
chunk_text: This chunk presents findings from a breast cancer prognostic study comparing invasive lobular carcinoma (ILC) and invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC). Mixed tumours were classified as ductal [S1]. The study found that grade 2 ILC had consistently poorer prognosis compared to grade 2 IDC [S4], with this difference persisting even when analyses were restricted to tumours with presumed favourable biomarkers [S4]. HER2 expression showed limited prognostic value in ILC due to the low frequency of HER2 expression in this subtype [S3]. The authors propose that lobular lesions represent a distinct family of neoplastic lesions in the breast [S6], and suggest that E-cadherin may be more useful than histological grade for prognostication and treatment determination in ILC [S7]. The study was limited by the low number of lobular tumours available for analysis [S5].

claim: Positive tissue control: normal tonsil included in each staining run; negative control: primary antibody omitted
chunk_text: This chunk describes the methodological framework for Ki67 IHC assessment in a surgical resection cohort. No patients received neoadjuvant therapy [S1]. Histological review used ≥3–4 H&E sections per case to identify the representative section with the highest tumour burden and grade [S2]. Full-face sections were cut from FFPE resection specimens [S3]. IHC was performed automatically using the clinically-validated DAKO Cytomation EnVision+ system [S4], with antigen retrieval via citrate buffer (pH 6.0) microwave treatment [S5]. The primary antibody was anti-human Ki67 monoclonal antibody MIB1 (DAKO), incubated for 30 minutes [S6]. Each staining run included a normal tonsil positive control and a no-primary-antibody negative control [S7]. Ki67 was scored by visual light microscopy (ECLIPSE Ni-U; Nikon; 10x ocular, 40x objective; field diameter 0.63 mm) [S8]. Only invasive tumour cells were scored; necrosis, poor-quality areas, inviable tissue, DCIS, and inflammatory cells were excluded [S9]. Ki67 positivity was expressed as a percentage using multiple scoring methods (details truncated at chunk boundary) [S10].

claim: Ki67 positivity scoring method 2: average estimation of Ki67 within a defined hotspot
chunk_text: This chunk introduces a study (PMC9826086) evaluating Ki67 scoring methods in a luminal breast cancer cohort (n=1662). Ki67 is established as a marker of proliferation activity in breast cancer [S5], though no optimal clinical assessment method has been robustly defined [S6]. Sections were immunohistochemically stained for Ki67 and assessed for percentage, pattern, and intensity of expression [S8]. Three scoring methods were compared: (i) counting Ki67-positive cells among 1000 invasive tumour cells within a hotspot, (ii) average estimation within a defined hotspot, and (iii) average estimation across the whole section [S9]. Evaluation criteria included scoring time, interobserver agreement, and association with clinical outcome [S10].

claim: Cases classified into histopathological type and grade

The study included 727 cases of invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC) of no special type and invasive lobular carcinoma (ILC) [S4|PMC4329418_his0066-0409|69937], with 867 tissue samples suitable for tissue microarray (TMA) construction [S2|PMC4329418_his0066-0409|69937]. HER2 gene amplification status was assessed using chromogenic in-situ hybridization (CISH) [S9|PMC4329418_his0066-0409|69938], and E-cadherin (E-cad) staining was also performed [S10|PMC4329418_his0066-0409|69938]. Survival data were generated through linkage with the Cause of Death Registry of Norway and the Norwegian Cancer Registry [S3|PMC4329418_his0066-0409|69937].

claim: PhH3 superior to MAI in prognostic value for histological grading (HR 9.6 vs 3.6)
chunk_text: This chunk (C17) from PMC7539961_HIS-77-579 summarises key conclusions regarding PhH3 as a proliferation marker in breast cancer histological grading. Using PhH3 instead of the mitotic activity index (MAI) to determine the modified Bloom–Richardson (BR) grade resulted in grade upgrading in 14–27% of cases [S1]. PhH3 demonstrated independent prognostic value with a hazard ratio of 9.6, substantially exceeding the MAI's HR of 3.6 [S3], supporting the concept of replacing MAI with PhH3 to improve grading prognostic value [S4]. However, larger studies are needed before PhH3-based mitotic indices can be recommended for clinical practice [S5]. The study provided a unique comparison of reproducibility between traditional and novel proliferation markers, with reliable interobserver agreement across three dedicated breast pathologists at different institutions [S6, S7]. Importantly, the cohort was restricted to ER+ cancers [S8], a subset where proliferation assessment optimisation is particularly relevant given the use of genomic profiling to guide adjuvant chemotherapy decisions [S9]. Prognostic value of the proliferation markers could not be formally assessed due to unavailable and insufficient follow-up data [S10].

claim: Ki67 quantification method (hotspot counting) -> longest method timewise compared to other two Ki67 scoring methods
chunk_text: This chunk discusses the comparative performance of Ki67 scoring methods. High Ki67 expression, regardless of assessment method, was significantly associated with aggressive tumour behaviour parameters including higher grade, larger tumour size, LVI, and lymph node invasion [S6|PMC9826086_HIS-81-786|70087]. Among methods, the hotspot quantification method (counting Ki67-positive cells among 1000 invasive tumour cells within the hotspot) demonstrated the best association with these parameters [S6], the highest interobserver concordance, and the most accurate patient outcome prediction [S8|PMC9826086_HIS-81-786|70087], despite being the most time-consuming method. The hotspot is identified as containing the highest proliferative pool driving tumour behaviour [S7|PMC9826086_HIS-81-786|70087]. A prior unpublished study (n=610) found that counting 1000 cells in randomly selected areas showed significant discrepancy versus established methods and was not associated with patient outcome [S3–S5|PMC9826086_HIS-81-786|70086]. Ultimately, Ki67 hotspot quantification showed the highest hazard ratio, lowest P value, and independent prognostic value for disease outcome compared to the other two methods [S10|PMC9826086_HIS-81-786|70088].

claim: PhH3-based grading: minority of patients downgraded from grade II → grade I (n=1, 2, 3 for observers 1, 2, 3) or grade III → grade II (n=1, 2, 6 for observers 1, 2, 3)
chunk_text: This chunk (C12) from PMC7539961_HIS-77-579 reports interobserver reproducibility data for three proliferation markers in luminal-type breast cancer grading. PhH3 categorical scoring showed substantial interobserver agreement (κ = 0.68–0.80) [S1–S2], whereas Ki67 (κ = 0.55) and MAI (κ = 0.26–0.52) achieved only fair-to-moderate agreement [S3]. When PhH3 replaced MAI in the modified Nottingham grading scheme, interobserver agreement for histological grade improved (PhH3 κ = 0.48–0.52 vs MAI κ = 0.32–0.43) [S5]. PhH3-based grading predominantly upgraded patients: grade I→II in 4–12% and grade II→III in 14–27% (P < 0.001) [S6], with only a small number downgraded [S7]. Among those upgraded from grade II→III, the majority had PhH3 ≥13 (69–95%), while a substantial proportion of grade I→II shifts had PhH3 <13 (31–83%) [S8]. The authors conclude that PhH3-based mitotic counting is more reproducible than MAI or Ki67 for assessing tumour proliferation in ER+ early breast cancer [S9–S10].

claim: NY-ESO-1 expression exclusively in TN/basal-like tumours (100% of NY-ESO-1-positive TN tumours are TN/basal-like)
chunk_text: This chunk from PMC6635746_HIS-73-68 reports on the co-expression and clinicopathological associations of cancer-testis antigens (CTAs) MAGE-A and NY-ESO-1 in breast cancer. All 14 NY-ESO-1-positive cases co-expressed MAGE-A (P = 2.06 × 10⁻⁹) [S2]. Both CTAs were associated with Ki67 expression and tumour grade (driven primarily by mitotic score) [S3–S4]. Expression was strongly enriched in triple-negative (TN) tumours: 86% of MAGE-A-positive TN cases were TN/basal-like, and 100% of NY-ESO-1-positive TN cases were TN/basal-like [S5]. Within TNBC, both CTAs showed positive associations with c-Kit, p53, and mitosis-independent TTK expression [S6]. NY-ESO-1 (particularly) and MAGE-A were associated with vimentin expression and inversely associated with AR expression, though these associations did not reach significance within the TN subgroup [S7]. The cohort median overall survival was 13.6 years [S8]. MAGE-A-positive cases showed a 40% decrease in BCSS at 25 years in the whole cohort [S9], and a 35% decrease in BCSS at 5 years in the TN group (not statistically significant) [S9]. NY-ESO-1-positive cases trended towards poorer outcome, but this was not significant after accounting for TN status [S10].

claim: Grade 2 tumours comprised 51.9% of ductal tumours
chunk_text: This study aimed to compare breast cancer specific survival (BCSS) for invasive lobular carcinoma (ILC) and invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC), and to evaluate the prognostic value of histopathological grading of ILC and E-cadherin as a prognostic marker in ILC. The study included 116 lobular and 611 ductal breast carcinomas [S6|PMC4329418_his0066-0409|69929]. Grade 2 tumours constituted 85.3% of lobular tumours and 51.9% of ductal tumours [S10|PMC4329418_his0066-0409|69930].

claim: PHH3-H&E staining -> improves quality of diagnosis
chunk_text: This chunk evaluates the technical and diagnostic advantages of PHH3-H&E dual staining for mitotic counting in histopathology. The study found that PHH3-H&E dual staining achieved the highest interobserver agreement for mitotic figure recognition [S1], with mitotic counts being dramatically undercounted when H&E stain was used alone [S2]. PHH3 staining showed heterogenous distribution within tumours and enabled easy identification of mitotic hotspots [S3], while being significantly less time-consuming than conventional H&E mitotic counting and improving diagnostic throughput and quality [S3-S4]. The dual staining approach allows simultaneous assessment of mitotic morphology and tumour histological features, increasing quantification specificity [S5]. A key advantage is that PHH3-H&E dual staining preserves diagnostic tissue areas that would otherwise be lost during sequential sectioning, particularly important for limited core needle biopsies [S6-S7]. Unlike sequential staining protocols that may compromise epitope integrity, IHC-H&E dual staining on the same slide without destaining preserves tissue without requiring sequential cutting [S8-S9]. Integration with whole slide imaging (WSI) and artificial intelligence enables objective measurements via digital image analysis (DIA) for more accurate and objective grade reporting [S10].

claim: Cell-to-cell adhesion involves cytoplasmic catenins and actin cytoskeleton, implying better prognosis for ILC compared to IDC
chunk_text: Prognostic differences between ILC and IDC are noted, with E-cadherin expression serving as a potential prognostic marker. E-cadherin positivity correlates with better prognosis in ILC, while loss of E-cadherin is associated with invasion and metastasis. Future validation of E-cadherin's prognostic utility could expand its clinical use, and cellular adhesion mechanisms involving catenins and actin are implicated in prognosis. HER2 positivity is rare in ILC, limiting its prognostic value. Overall, better prognostic markers for ILC are needed [S1|PMC4329418_his0066-0409|69954-69956].

claim: No patients in cohort received neoadjuvant therapy
chunk_text: This chunk describes the rationale and methodology of a large cohort study examining Ki67 assessment in breast cancer. Ki67 scoring lacks a standardised method, leading to challenges in consistency, reproducibility, and reliability [S1|PMC9826086_HIS-81-786|70057], and the optimal low/high dichotomisation cutoff remains undefined and highly variable in the literature [S2|PMC9826086_HIS-81-786|70057]. The study aims to compare multiple visual Ki67 assessment methods across dimensions including practicality, reproducibility, prognostic/predictive value, and biological significance of staining intensities, patterns, and sublocalisations in a large luminal ER-positive, HER2-negative BC cohort [S3|PMC9826086_HIS-81-786|70057]. The cohort comprised n=1662 ER-positive, HER2-negative BC patients with Nottingham LN stage 1 or 2 [S4|PMC9826086_HIS-81-786|70058], with detailed clinicopathological data available for 1583 patients [S5|PMC9826086_HIS-81-786|70058]. Outcome endpoints were BCSS and DMFS [S6|PMC9826086_HIS-81-786|70058]. ER, PR, and HER2 data were sourced from original pathology reports [S7|PMC9826086_HIS-81-786|70058]. Treatment exposure included endocrine therapy in 90% and chemotherapy in 17% of patients; no patient received neoadjuvant therapy [S8–S9|PMC9826086_HIS-81-786|70058]. For Ki67 assessment, at least 3–4 H&E sections per case were reviewed to select the most representative section with highest tumour burden and histological grade [S10|PMC9826086_HIS-81-786|70058].

claim: Grade 2 tumours comprise 51.9% of ductal tumours.
chunk_text: Grade 2 tumours constitute 85.3% of lobular tumours and 51.9% of ductal tumours [S2|PMC4329418_his0066-0409|69930]. Breast cancer specific survival (BCSS) in ILC grade 2 is comparable to that in IDC grade 3 [S3|PMC4329418_his0066-0409|69930]. Loss of cell-to-cell cohesion is a common feature in ILC variants [S9|PMC4329418_his0066-0409|69932]. Histopathological grade is recognized as an important prognostic tool [S10|PMC4329418_his0066-0409|69933].

claim: Aberrant staining (cytoplasmic staining or intermittent membranous staining) classified as negative.
chunk_text: IHC evaluations were performed independently by two researchers. ER and PR were positive if ≥ 1% of the tumour cells showed positive nuclear staining [S2|PMC4329418_his0066-0409|69940]. Ki67 was classified as high if ≥ 15% stained nuclei and low if < 15% [S3|PMC4329418_his0066-0409|69940]. CK5 and EGFR staining index of 0 -1 was considered negative and 2 -9 was considered positive [S4|PMC4329418_his0066-0409|69940]. In cases where CISH failed, + 3 IHC staining for HER2 was recorded as positive [S6|PMC4329418_his0066-0409|69940]. Kaplan-Meier methods were used to estimate BCSS for ILC grade 2 compared to IDC grades 1 and 3, and to compare survival of ILC and IDC grade 2, E-cad + and E-cad /C0 tumours [S10|PMC4329418_his0066-0409|69941].

claim: Ki67 positivity by average estimation within hotspot yields mean 14%
chunk_text: This chunk evaluates three methods for assessing Ki67 expression in breast cancer [S1|PMC9826086_HIS-81-786|70050]. The quantification method counting positive cells among 1000 invasive tumour cells within hotspot yielded a mean Ki67 expression of 16%, compared to 14% for average estimation within hotspot and 12% for whole-slide average estimation [S3|PMC9826086_HIS-81-786|70051]. The 1000-cell quantification method demonstrated the highest interobserver agreement and the strongest association with patient outcome, independent of the other two methods [S4|PMC9826086_HIS-81-786|70051]. A granular pattern of Ki67 expression was associated with poorer clinical outcomes compared to other expression patterns [S5|PMC9826086_HIS-81-786|70051]. claim: Ki67 H-score -> significant association with shorter DMFS only; no significant association with other patient outcomes
chunk_text: This chunk (C14, PMC9826086_HIS-81-786) reports prognostic analyses of Ki67 scoring methods in breast cancer. In multivariate analysis, hotspot quantification of Ki67-positive cells among 1000 tumour cells was the only method providing statistically significant independent prognostic value across all cutoffs [S1]. Average Ki67 estimation within the hotspot showed only a weak independent association with BCSS (HR=1.6, 95% CI 1.1–2.4, P=0.018) at the 10% cutoff, losing significance at other thresholds [S2]. In the adjuvant therapy context, high Ki67 was significantly associated with poor outcome in endocrine-treated patients regardless of scoring method [S3], with hotspot quantification again showing independent prognostic superiority in multivariate analysis [S4]. claim: MAGE-A expression -> strong association with TTK (spindle assembly checkpoint protein) expression, independent of mitosis
chunk_text: This chunk discusses the molecular and immunohistochemical relationships between cancer-testis antigens (CTAs), p53, chromosomal instability (CIN), and tumour differentiation in breast cancer. p53 mutations produce a stable non-functional nuclear protein that mimics overexpression by IHC, making p53 IHC overexpression a surrogate for functional abrogation [S1|PMC6635746_HIS-73-68|69992]. p53 inadequacy contributes to CIN and aneuploidy [S2], which in turn promotes aberrant DNA damage repair and mutagenesis [S3]. NY-ESO-1-positive tumours show coexpression with p53, implying chromosomal abnormalities and a proliferative advantage [S4]. In contrast, MAGE-A shows no association with p53 [S5], possibly because MAGE-A inhibits p53 function by blocking its interaction with chromatin [S5]. MAGE-A expression is strongly associated with mitosis-independent TTK expression, a spindle assembly checkpoint protein and CIN marker in TNBC [S6]. CTA re-expression is thought to confer stem cell-like properties [S7], and both NY-ESO-1 and MAGE-A show striking coexpression with the luminal progenitor marker c-Kit [S8] and enrichment with vimentin [S9], suggesting primitive differentiation states. Basal-like breast cancers frequently exhibit luminal progenitor-like phenotypes and may originate from this cell type [S10].

claim: Using MAI for histological grading had lower interobserver agreement j scores of 0.43, 0.35, and 0.32
chunk_text: PhH3-positive cells were counted in a 2 mm2 area with a threshold of ≥13 cells to distinguish low- from high-proliferative tumours in luminal-type breast cancer [S2]. Ki67 expression was assessed using a global scoring method, with percentages below 20% considered low proliferation [S3,S4]. Counting PhH3-positive cells showed high reproducibility among three observers with an ICC of 0.86 and substantial interobserver agreement (j scores 0.78, 0.68, 0.80), outperforming MAI and Ki67 which showed fair to moderate agreement [S7,S8]. Using PhH3 for histological grading increased interobserver agreement (j scores 0.52, 0.48, 0.52) and increased the proportion of grade III tumours (14%, 18%, 27%) compared to MAI-based grading [S9]. Overall, PhH3 outperforms Ki67 and MAI as a reproducible measure of tumour proliferation in luminal-type breast cancer [S10].

claim: Ki67 quantification method (hotspot counting) -> most accurate method for predicting patient outcome among Ki67 scoring methods
chunk_text: This chunk discusses the comparative performance of Ki67 scoring methods. High Ki67 expression, regardless of assessment method, was significantly associated with aggressive tumour behaviour parameters including higher grade, larger tumour size, LVI, and lymph node invasion [S6|PMC9826086_HIS-81-786|70087]. Among methods, the hotspot quantification method (counting Ki67-positive cells among 1000 invasive tumour cells within the hotspot) demonstrated the best association with these parameters [S6], the highest interobserver concordance, and the most accurate patient outcome prediction [S8|PMC9826086_HIS-81-786|70087], despite being the most time-consuming method. The hotspot is identified as containing the highest proliferative pool driving tumour behaviour [S7|PMC9826086_HIS-81-786|70087]. A prior unpublished study (n=610) found that counting 1000 cells in randomly selected areas showed significant discrepancy versus established methods and was not associated with patient outcome [S3–S5|PMC9826086_HIS-81-786|70086]. Ultimately, Ki67 hotspot quantification showed the highest hazard ratio, lowest P value, and independent prognostic value for disease outcome compared to the other two methods [S10|PMC9826086_HIS-81-786|70088].

claim: Category 1 tumours are well-differentiated with inherently good prognosis
chunk_text: Tumours are classified into three categories based on histological feature scores, with category 1 tumours being well-differentiated and having a good prognosis, and category 3 tumours being poorly differentiated [S1|PMC7539961_HIS-77-579|70009, S2|PMC7539961_HIS-77-579|70009]. Histological grade assessment provides important prognostic information worldwide to guide systemic treatment decisions [S3|PMC7539961_HIS-77-579|70010]. Patients with grade 3 tumours are candidates for adjuvant chemotherapy, whereas those with grade 1 tumours are candidates for less toxic hormonal therapy [S4|PMC7539961_HIS-77-579|70010]. Approximately 30-60% of patients are diagnosed with grade 2 tumours, where the indication for adjuvant systemic treatment is less clear and interobserver grading variability is high [S5|PMC7539961_HIS-77-579|70010, S6|PMC7539961_HIS-77-579|70010]. Tumour proliferation-related genes functionally result in cell division, which is detectable as mitotic figures with typical chromosome sets by pathologists [S9|PMC7539961_HIS-77-579|70011, S10|PMC7539961_HIS-77-579|70011].

claim: Nottingham grade 1 (category 1) = well-differentiated tumours with inherently good prognosis; grade 3 (category 3) = poorly differentiated tumours
chunk_text: This chunk reports findings on the use of phosphohistone H3 (PhH3) as a proliferation marker for histological grading in breast cancer. PhH3-based grading demonstrated higher inter-observer agreement (kappa 0.52, 0.48, 0.52) compared to the mitotic activity index (MAI; kappa 0.43, 0.35, 0.32) [S1|PMC7539961_HIS-77-579|70005], and PhH3 was concluded to outperform both Ki67 and MAI as a reproducible measure of tumour proliferation in luminal-type breast cancer [S2|PMC7539961_HIS-77-579|70006]. However, PhH3 use increased the proportion of grade III tumours (14%, 18%, 27%) [S1|PMC7539961_HIS-77-579|70005] and would result in more high-grade cancer classifications [S3|PMC7539961_HIS-77-579|70006]. Contextually, histological grade is established as one of the most robust prognostic factors in breast cancer [S4|PMC7539961_HIS-77-579|70007], with the Nottingham (Bloom-Richardson) grading system incorporating nuclear polymorphism, tubular formation, and mitotic count — the latter reflecting tumour proliferation [S8|PMC7539961_HIS-77-579|70009]. Grade 1 tumours are well-differentiated with good prognosis, while grade 3 tumours are poorly differentiated [S10|PMC7539961_HIS-77-579|70009].

claim: MAI has independent prognostic value with HR 3.6 (inferior to PhH3 HR 9.6)
chunk_text: This chunk (C17) from PMC7539961_HIS-77-579 summarises key conclusions regarding PhH3 as a proliferation marker in breast cancer histological grading. Using PhH3 instead of the mitotic activity index (MAI) to determine the modified Bloom–Richardson (BR) grade resulted in grade upgrading in 14–27% of cases [S1]. PhH3 demonstrated independent prognostic value with a hazard ratio of 9.6, substantially exceeding the MAI's HR of 3.6 [S3], supporting the concept of replacing MAI with PhH3 to improve grading prognostic value [S4]. However, larger studies are needed before PhH3-based mitotic indices can be recommended for clinical practice [S5]. The study provided a unique comparison of reproducibility between traditional and novel proliferation markers, with reliable interobserver agreement across three dedicated breast pathologists at different institutions [S6, S7]. Importantly, the cohort was restricted to ER+ cancers [S8], a subset where proliferation assessment optimisation is particularly relevant given the use of genomic profiling to guide adjuvant chemotherapy decisions [S9]. Prognostic value of the proliferation markers could not be formally assessed due to unavailable and insufficient follow-up data [S10].

claim: PHH3-H&E staining -> increases number of cases diagnosed daily
chunk_text: This chunk evaluates the technical and diagnostic advantages of PHH3-H&E dual staining for mitotic counting in histopathology. The study found that PHH3-H&E dual staining achieved the highest interobserver agreement for mitotic figure recognition [S1], with mitotic counts being dramatically undercounted when H&E stain was used alone [S2]. PHH3 staining showed heterogenous distribution within tumours and enabled easy identification of mitotic hotspots [S3], while being significantly less time-consuming than conventional H&E mitotic counting and improving diagnostic throughput and quality [S3-S4]. The dual staining approach allows simultaneous assessment of mitotic morphology and tumour histological features, increasing quantification specificity [S5]. A key advantage is that PHH3-H&E dual staining preserves diagnostic tissue areas that would otherwise be lost during sequential sectioning, particularly important for limited core needle biopsies [S6-S7]. Unlike sequential staining protocols that may compromise epitope integrity, IHC-H&E dual staining on the same slide without destaining preserves tissue without requiring sequential cutting [S8-S9]. Integration with whole slide imaging (WSI) and artificial intelligence enables objective measurements via digital image analysis (DIA) for more accurate and objective grade reporting [S10].

claim: Ki67 is expressed in all phases of the cell cycle and is not specific for mitosis in breast cancer
chunk_text: In breast cancer, mitotic count per 3 mm2 shows a significant positive association with PHH3 score, whereas Ki67 score shows only a mild positive correlation with mitotic count [S1|PMC10100421_HIS-82-393|69915]. Ki67 is expressed in all phases of the cell cycle and is not specific for mitosis, with many non-mitotic cells positive for Ki67 [S2|PMC10100421_HIS-82-393|69915; S3|PMC10100421_HIS-82-393|69915]. In contrast, PHH3 specifically identifies cells undergoing mitosis and provides a better representation of proliferation activity than Ki67 [S4|PMC10100421_HIS-82-393|69915]. PHH3 is an independent predictor of survival when added to grade and nodal stage and shows a more significant association with survival than mitosis score and Ki67 in multivariate analysis, suggesting it could be more predictive of outcome [S5|PMC10100421_HIS-82-393|69916]. PHH3 has been proposed as a replacement for the Ki67 index in several cancers [S6|PMC10100421_HIS-82-393|69916]. However, implementation of PHH3 staining in routine practice may face cost burden challenges [S8|PMC10100421_HIS-82-393|69917].

claim: Substituting PhH3 for MAI in Nottingham grading: grade I → grade II shift in 8% (obs1), 12% (obs2), 4% (obs3) of patients (P < 0.001)
chunk_text: This chunk (C12) from PMC7539961_HIS-77-579 reports interobserver reproducibility data for three proliferation markers in luminal-type breast cancer grading. PhH3 categorical scoring showed substantial interobserver agreement (κ = 0.68–0.80) [S1–S2], whereas Ki67 (κ = 0.55) and MAI (κ = 0.26–0.52) achieved only fair-to-moderate agreement [S3]. claim: Grade 2 ILC prognosis comparable to grade 3 IDC
chunk_text: This cohort study of breast cancer patients with long-term follow-up demonstrates that grade 2 invasive lobular carcinoma (ILC) has significantly poorer prognosis compared to grade 2 invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC) [S5], with grade 2 ILC prognosis comparable to grade 3 IDC [S6]. This pattern persists when analyses are restricted to tumours with favourable prognostic markers (ER+, HER2-, Ki67 low) [S7]. E-cadherin expression emerges as a favourable prognostic marker specifically in ILC [S8]. The difference between luminal A IDC and ILC subtypes was statistically significant [S1]. The authors note that morphological features of ILC differ from IDC [S10], which may explain why histological grade has different prognostic significance in ILC compared to IDC [S10]. Adjustment for age, stage, and time-period did not influence these results [S4].

claim: Inter-rater reliability for categorical PhH3, Ki67, and MAI (threshold-based) assessed using Cohen's kappa
chunk_text: This chunk describes the methodological framework for PhH3 and Ki67 proliferation marker assessment and inter-rater reliability analysis. PhH3 mitotic counts were performed in a 2 mm² area at the zone of highest proliferation (preferably tumour periphery), counting only morphologically mitotic PhH3-positive objects and excluding fine granular nuclear staining (G2 phase) [S1–S2|PMC7539961_HIS-77-579|70017]. A previously validated PhH3 threshold of ≥13 positive cells/2 mm² was applied to stratify patients, with 20-year recurrence-free survival rates for distant metastases of 58% (high group) vs. 96% (low group) [S3|PMC7539961_HIS-77-579|70017]. Ki67 was assessed in 105 patients using the global scoring method, with a 20% positivity cut-off distinguishing high- from low-proliferative tumours [S4–S6|PMC7539961_HIS-77-579|70018]. Inter-rater agreement for continuous scores (PhH3, Ki67, MAI) was evaluated by ICC (two-way random effects model), and Cohen's kappa was used for categorical variables [S8|PMC7539961_HIS-77-579|70019]. An alternative histological grade was constructed by substituting the MAI component with PhH3 scores (1 point: ≤7; 2 points: 8–12; 3 points: ≥13 per 2 mm²) and compared to the traditional MAI-based grade via chi-square test [S9–S10|PMC7539961_HIS-77-579|70019].

In multivariate analysis, hotspot quantification of Ki67-positive cells among 1000 tumour cells was the only method providing statistically significant independent prognostic value across all cutoffs [S1]. Average Ki67 estimation within the hotspot showed only a weak independent association with BCSS (HR=1.6, 95% CI 1.1–2.4, P=0.018) at the 10% cutoff, losing significance at other thresholds [S2]. In the adjuvant therapy context, high Ki67 was significantly associated with poor outcome in endocrine-treated patients regardless of scoring method [S3], with hotspot quantification again showing independent prognostic superiority in multivariate analysis [S4]. claim: Occasional cytoplasmic and/or cell membrane staining of Ki67 not included in assessment
verbatim_support: Ki67 is a nuclear protein that is expressed during all cell cycle phases except G0. Visual assessment of Ki67 immunohistochemically stained BC tissue sections is considered the standard method for Ki67 evaluation, but this approach is timeand costintensive. Ki67 is expressed mainly in the nuclei of the proliferating cells or demarcates the chromatin spindles of the cells in the mitotic phase. Despite the presence of several methods for Ki67, there is a consensus that any nuclear and/or mitotic spindle staining should be considered in the final score regardless the intensity or the pattern of the staining. Occasional cytoplasmic and/or cell membrane staining of Ki67 can be observed but are not included in the Ki67 assessment. Staining usually has several intensities ranging from faint to strong, and various patterns including homogenous, coarse-granular, fine granular/dotted, nuclear membrane, subnuclear membrane condensations, nucleolar, and a mixture of all the aforementioned patterns, which occurs in the majority of cases.

chunk_text: This methodological section describes Ki67 proliferation assessment strategies in breast cancer histopathology. Multiple Ki67 cutoff thresholds (10%, 14%, 20%, 30%) were employed to categorize tumours into high and low proliferation groups [S1]. Overall, MAGE-A was expressed in 13% and NY-ESO-1 in 3.8% of all cases [S5, S9], but expression was markedly enriched in TN breast cancer (~47% and ~17%, respectively) [S9]. Both CTAs were strongly associated with the TN phenotype (P < 0.0001) [S6], and NY-ESO-1-positive cases co-expressed MAGE-A (P = 2.06 × 10⁻⁹) [S6]. CTA-positive tumours were the most proliferative and poorly differentiated, showing genomic instability [S6], and were characterised by co-expression of c-Kit and TTK and overexpression of p53 [S7]. Approximately 85% of positive cases showed homogeneous staining (>75% of tumour cells) [S5], supporting IHC of tissue biopsies as a reliable companion biomarker [S10]. The authors conclude that targeting MAGE-A and NY-ESO-1 via immunotherapy is feasible in TN breast cancer [S9].
